Wilt Chamberlain.text: Once gathered 55 rebounds in a game, and never fouled out in his career.
Wilt Chamberlain.evidence: He also once gathered 55 rebounds, and never fouled out.

Bill Russell.text: Won 11 titles in 13 seasons, and as player-coach became the first black NBA coach to win a championship.
Bill Russell.evidence: He was the centerpiece of the Celtics dynasty that played for 12 NBA championships and won 11 during his 13-year career. ... During the final three seasons of his career (1966–1969), he served as player-coach of the Celtics, becoming the first black NBA coach to win a championship.

Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.text: As Lew Alcindor, he led his New York City high school to 71 consecutive wins.
Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.evidence: Abdul-Jabbar was known as Lew Alcindor when he played at Power Memorial, a private Catholic high school in New York City, where he led their team to 71 consecutive wins.

Elvin Hayes.text: His 222 rebounds in the NCAA tournament are still the most by any player.
Elvin Hayes.evidence: His 222 rebounds in the NCAA tournament is still the most by a player in history.

Moses Malone.text: Nicknamed the "Chairman of the Boards", he retired as the all-time leader in offensive rebounds.
Moses Malone.evidence: Nicknamed the "Chairman of the Boards" for his rebounding prowess, he finished his career as the all-time leader in offensive rebounds after leading both the ABA and NBA in the category a combined nine times.

Tim Duncan.text: Wanted to be a swimmer until Hurricane Hugo destroyed his island's only Olympic-sized pool.
Tim Duncan.evidence: Born and raised on Saint Croix in the U.S. Virgin Islands, Duncan initially aspired to be a competitive swimmer, but took up basketball at 14 after Hurricane Hugo destroyed the island's only Olympic-sized pool.

Karl Malone.text: Appeared in the playoffs in every season of his 18-season career.
Karl Malone.evidence: Karl Anthony Malone (born July 24, 1963), nicknamed "the Mailman", is an American former professional basketball player who played in the National Basketball Association (NBA) for 18 seasons with the Utah Jazz, and in his last season, the Los Angeles Lakers. ... Malone appeared in the playoffs every season in his career, including the NBA Finals in 1997 and 1998 with the Jazz.

Robert Parish.text: Wore No. 00 because, seen as the worst player on his junior high team, he got the last jersey left.
Robert Parish.evidence: Parish was already 6 ft 6 in (1.98 m) tall in the seventh grade (age 12–13) when junior high coach Coleman Kidd first noticed him and encouraged him to play basketball, which was new to him. ... It was at this time that Parish started wearing his uniform No. 00. The players got to choose their jerseys in order of perceived ability and since Parish was viewed as the worst player, he received the last remaining jersey, which was number 00.

Kevin Garnett.text: Made his feature film debut in Uncut Gems, playing a fictionalized version of himself.
Kevin Garnett.evidence: Garnett made his feature film debut in the 2019 crime thriller Uncut Gems, playing a fictionalized version of himself.

Dwight Howard.text: After the 2021-22 NBA season he moved overseas to the T1 League's Taoyuan Leopards and was named a T1 All-Star.
Dwight Howard.evidence: After the 2021–22 NBA season, Howard moved overseas and signed with the Taoyuan Leopards of the T1 League. In his lone season with the team, he was named a T1 All-Star.
